feature: HLA-restricted immunotherapy handles (HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T, WT1, PRAME) - the primary reason for this Libby run
test_name: High-resolution (4-digit) HLA class I typing of HLA-A, -B and -C in the patient and the HLA-identical sibling donor
tissue_type: whole blood; archived allele-level 2020 typing report acceptable
rationale: Resolves the 4-digit HLA-A*02:01 and A*24:02 status that every HLA-restricted option named for this case sits behind: TSC-100/TSC-101 (NCT05473910), the Fred Hutch HA-1 TCR-T (NCT03326921) and BSB-1001 (NCT06704152) each require HLA-A*02:01, and A*24:02 keeps a WT1-siTCR route open if A*02:01 is negative. High-resolution typing was performed for the 2020 sibling transplant but sits in the record as a placeholder, so pull the allele-level report from the transplant and donor-registry file first and re-type on a fresh draw only if it cannot be produced quickly. Type the sibling donor in the same pass; until an allele call exists the question this case was submitted to answer cannot be scoped in either direction.
turnaround_estimate: days if the 2020 report is retrievable; 3-7 days for new NGS typing, STAT available
tissue_required_estimate: 5-10 mL whole blood (EDTA) from the patient and from the sibling donor; buccal swab acceptable for the donor
decision_gated: TSC-100/TSC-101 (NCT05473910), Fred Hutch HA-1 TCR-T (NCT03326921) and BSB-1001 (NCT06704152), all of which require HLA-A*02:01

providers.name: HistoGenetics
providers.notes: Highest-volume US HLA sequence-based typing laboratory (ASHI and CLIA accredited), which is why it is the default pick for a fast allele-level answer. If the treating transplant centre runs its own ASHI-accredited laboratory, sending there is usually faster still.

providers.name: Versiti Diagnostic Laboratories
providers.notes: ASHI-accredited; also runs the chimerism and HLA loss-of-heterozygosity work this case needs, so one account covers three orders.

providers.name: ARUP Laboratories
providers.address: 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108

notes: The fastest path is a records request, not a new assay. Ask the 2020 transplant centre and the donor registry for the allele-level typing report for both the patient and the donor before drawing anything.

feature: HLA-restricted immunotherapy handles (HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T, WT1, PRAME) - the primary reason for this Libby run
test_name: HA-1 / HA-2 minor histocompatibility antigen genotyping (HMHA1 rs1801284 and MYO1G) in the patient and the sibling donor
tissue_type: whole blood from patient and donor
rationale: Establishes the recipient-positive / donor-negative disparity that HA-directed TCR-T requires. NCT03326921 enrolls recipients carrying the HA-1(H) genotype (rs1801284 A/G or A/A) whose donor is HA-1(H) negative (G/G); NCT05473910 requires an HA-1-positive genotype for TSC-100 and an HA-2-positive genotype for TSC-101; NCT06704152 requires HA-1 H/H or H/R with an HA-1-negative donor. HLA-identical siblings can still differ at these minor loci, so a patient-only result leaves eligibility undetermined, and the donor sample and consent are the slow step worth starting now.
turnaround_estimate: 1-3 weeks as a specialised send-out or through trial screening
tissue_required_estimate: 5-10 mL whole blood (EDTA) from the patient and from the sibling donor; buccal swab acceptable for the donor
decision_gated: TSC-100/TSC-101 (NCT05473910), Fred Hutch HA-1 TCR-T (NCT03326921) and BSB-1001 (NCT06704152); all require recipient HA-1-positive with an HA-1-negative donor

providers.name: Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center (Immunogenetics / Bleakley HA-1 program)
providers.notes: Developed the HA-1 TCR-T platform and performs the HA-1 genotyping for NCT03326921, so it runs this assay routinely rather than case-by-case. Preferred on that turnaround argument, not on size.

providers.name: TScan Therapeutics (ALLOHA trial screening)
providers.notes: ALLOHA (NCT05473910) screening includes central HA-1 and HA-2 genotyping of patient and donor; contacting the study team can substitute for a separate send-out.

providers.name: Versiti Diagnostic Laboratories
providers.notes: ASHI-accredited immunogenetics laboratory; HA-1/HA-2 is not on the published catalogue, so confirm availability before shipping.

providers.name: HistoGenetics
providers.notes: High-volume HLA and immunogenetics laboratory; ask specifically whether minor histocompatibility antigen genotyping can be run as a custom order.

notes: HA-1/HA-2 genotyping is not a routine catalogue test at US commercial reference laboratories, so treat availability as something to confirm by phone rather than assume. Routing through a trial's central screening is often the practical answer.

test_name: Retrieval of the 2019 diagnostic TP53 variant identity and VAF from the original NGS report
tissue_type: no new specimen; archived 2019 report and variant call file
rationale: Recovers the exact amino-acid change and VAF from the 2019 diagnostic NGS, which is the cheapest route to whether the founder TP53 lesion was Y220C. NCT06616636 (rezatapopt plus azacitidine in TP53 Y220C myeloid malignancies) requires a Y220C call by CLIA-approved local testing at VAF above 2 percent, so the specific variant rather than TP53 status in general is what opens or closes that door. This is a records request against an existing report, and it should happen before any conclusion is drawn from the 2026 negative result.
tissue_required_estimate: No new specimen. Request the annotated variant table (HGVS p. notation and VAF) from the 2019 testing laboratory
decision_gated: Rezatapopt plus azacitidine via NCT06616636, which is Y220C-contingent
notes: No provider row applies; this is a medical-records and laboratory-report request to whichever laboratory ran the 2019 diagnostic panel, not an assay to order.

test_name: Copy-number-capable myeloid NGS panel at relapse with TP53 variant-level reporting and VAF (Y220C determination)
tissue_type: fresh bone marrow aspirate; high-blast peripheral blood acceptable
rationale: Re-tests TP53 at relapse on an assay that can see what the 2026 panel could not: that panel ran at a 2 percent limit of detection with no copy-number calling and was not MRD-grade, so a subclonal or copy-loss TP53 event would have been reported as negative. A copy-number-capable panel reporting variant identity and VAF resolves the 2019-mutant versus 2026-negative discrepancy in whichever direction the biology actually runs, and a Y220C call above 2 percent VAF from a CLIA laboratory is the entry criterion for NCT06616636. Down-calling to TP53 wild-type on the 2026 result alone would discard both a possible rezatapopt handle and the adverse-risk assignment that shapes the transplant plan.
tissue_required_estimate: Fresh bone marrow aspirate at relapse (EDTA); peripheral blood acceptable given circulating blasts of 58-82 percent
decision_gated: Rezatapopt plus azacitidine via NCT06616636; also settles the TP53 adverse-risk assignment for HCT2 planning

providers.name: Foundation Medicine
providers.notes: FoundationOne Heme reports copy number alongside sequence variants on marrow or blood, which is the specific gap in the 2026 assay. Widely accepted for trial screening.

providers.name: Tempus
providers.address: 600 W Chicago Ave, Suite 510, Chicago, IL 60654

notes: Ask the laboratory to report VAF numerically and to state the assay's limit of detection and copy-number method on the report, since NCT06616636 screens on both variant identity and a VAF threshold. This is also the order that carries the MSI, TMB and fusion reads the biomarker survey deferred onto a comprehensive panel.

test_name: Quantitative CD123 (IL3RA) antigen-density flow cytometry reported as antibodies bound per cell (ABC) or MESF
tissue_type: fresh bone marrow aspirate or peripheral blood, viable cells
rationale: Turns the qualitative CD123-positive flow call into the surface-density number that CD123-directed agents are actually selected on. Reported CD123 density across AML spans roughly 200 to 10,000 molecules per cell, so a yes-or-no call cannot separate a strong handle from a marginal one, and both tagraxofusp and pivekimab sunirine carry BPDCN rather than AML labels, which puts the weight of any off-label or trial argument on the density read. Request ABC or MESF against calibrated beads explicitly, with the percentage of blasts positive alongside it; density is not a default readout on a phenotyping panel.
tissue_required_estimate: Fresh bone marrow aspirate or peripheral blood (sodium heparin or EDTA), viable cells, shipped same day
decision_gated: Tagraxofusp and pivekimab sunirine (CD123-directed), and dual CD33/CD123 strategies

providers.name: Hematologics, Inc.
providers.notes: A leukaemia-dedicated flow laboratory that works from a current specimen daily; preferred for turnaround on this specific assay. Confirm that quantitative density (ABC/MESF) is added, since it is a request rather than a default.

notes: Honest caveat: no validated CD123 density cutoff predicts benefit from tagraxofusp or pivekimab, so the number informs judgement rather than crossing a published threshold. It stays essential here because the profile makes actionability conditional on it and because neither agent is AML-labelled. Bundle the request with CD33 density and with the CLEC12A, CD70, LILRB4, CD37, CD200 and B7-H3 markers the biomarker survey put on the same panel.

test_name: Quantitative CD33 antigen-density flow cytometry reported as antibodies bound per cell (ABC) or MESF
tissue_type: fresh bone marrow aspirate or peripheral blood, viable cells
rationale: Turns the qualitative CD33-positive call into a density measure. In the central flow reanalysis of the randomised ALFA-0701 trial, benefit from gemtuzumab ozogamicin tracked with the level of blast CD33 expression rather than with positivity alone, so a low-density case that still reads positive is a weak handle for a CD33 antibody-drug conjugate. Order it on the same specimen as the CD123 density request; without it a gemtuzumab decision rests on an assay never sized to make it.
tissue_required_estimate: Fresh bone marrow aspirate or peripheral blood (sodium heparin or EDTA), viable cells; same specimen as the CD123 density request
decision_gated: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin (CD33 ADC) and dual CD33/CD123 targeting

providers.name: Hematologics, Inc.
providers.notes: Runs both the leukaemia flow work and the CD33 pharmacogenomic test, so the CD33 density and rs12459419 questions can be routed to one laboratory.

notes: The ALFA-0701 analysis reported benefit by expression level rather than by a validated cutoff, so report the number and interpret it against the laboratory's own AML range rather than against a published threshold.

feature: HLA-restricted immunotherapy handles (HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T, WT1, PRAME) - the primary reason for this Libby run
test_name: Quantitative WT1 transcript by the ELN-standardised RQ-PCR assay (WT1 copies per 10^4 ABL)
rationale: Confirms that the blasts overexpress WT1, the antigen behind the WT1-directed approaches this case names, and sets a quantitative baseline for tracking disease after any consolidation. The ELN-standardised assay has published reference thresholds of 250 copies per 10^4 ABL in marrow and 50 per 10^4 ABL in blood, so the number compares across centres instead of being laboratory-specific. Note that the WT1-C4 trial named in the profile (NCT01640301) has terminated, so this read currently confirms the target and supports MRD monitoring rather than unlocking a named product.
tissue_required_estimate: 2-3 mL bone marrow or 5-10 mL peripheral blood in EDTA, delivered within 24-48 hours for RNA integrity
decision_gated: WT1-directed T-cell approaches; also sets the standardised MRD baseline for post-HCT2 monitoring

providers.name: ARUP Laboratories
providers.address: 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108
providers.notes: Major US reference laboratory with a broad haematologic molecular menu and a straightforward send-out route; preferred as the routing point rather than because the assay is confirmed on its published catalogue.

providers.name: MD Anderson Cancer Center, Molecular Diagnostics Laboratory
providers.notes: Academic molecular diagnostics laboratory that publishes extensively on WT1 transcript monitoring in AML and runs NCT06616636, so one call can cover both questions.

notes: Availability is the real constraint: the ELN-standardised WT1 assay is not clearly listed on the major US commercial catalogues and several centres run it as a laboratory-developed test. Confirm by phone which version a laboratory offers and whether it reports copies per 10^4 ABL before shipping, because a non-standardised result will not compare to the published thresholds.

feature: HLA-restricted immunotherapy handles (HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T, WT1, PRAME) - the primary reason for this Libby run
test_name: PRAME expression on blasts by quantitative RT-PCR or RNA sequencing (reflex after HLA class I typing)
tissue_type: bone marrow aspirate or high-blast peripheral blood; FFPE clot acceptable for IHC
rationale: Answers whether these blasts express PRAME at all, which the record has never measured and which only becomes interpretable once HLA-A*02:01 status is known. Reported PRAME overexpression in AML varies widely with assay and cutoff, from roughly a third of cases in some series to 87 percent at first diagnosis in the Steger cohort, where the highest levels sat with unfavourable cytogenetics and with AML arising from myelodysplasia, which is this patient's history. MDG1011, the only PRAME TCR-T taken into myeloid disease, required HLA-A*02:01 plus PRAME mRNA detectable by qPCR and its trial (NCT03503968) has terminated, so run this as a reflex on tissue already being sent rather than as a standalone order.
tissue_required_estimate: Bone marrow aspirate or high-blast peripheral blood (EDTA); FFPE marrow clot section acceptable if IHC is used instead
decision_gated: PRAME-directed TCR-T or ImmTAC candidacy; reflex only if HLA-A*02:01 types positive

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Offers PRAME testing in a clinical format and accepts marrow specimens; preferred as the most accessible commercial route. Confirm which format the laboratory will run on a haematologic specimen, since the validated PRAME work is largely in melanoma.

providers.name: Tempus
providers.address: 600 W Chicago Ave, Suite 510, Chicago, IL 60654
providers.notes: Whole-transcriptome RNA sequencing reports PRAME expression alongside the fusion and expression reads the biomarker survey deferred.

providers.name: MD Anderson Cancer Center, Molecular Diagnostics Laboratory

notes: The biomarker survey called PRAME over-expressed in the large majority of AML. That is defensible on some series and not on others; the reported range is wide and cutoff-dependent, so quantify against the laboratory's own reference rather than treating positivity as a given. The secondary-AML association in the cited cohort argues for testing rather than against it.

test_name: Biopsy of the right-thigh myeloid sarcoma with CD33 and CD123 immunophenotyping plus targeted myeloid NGS
tissue_type: core biopsy of the extramedullary lesion; fresh tissue for flow plus FFPE for IHC and NGS
rationale: Tests whether the marrow immunophenotype and genotype speak for the extramedullary disease. In a meta-analysis of 85 studies, 56 percent of the 112 patients with paired myeloid sarcoma and marrow sequencing were discordant in mutational profile, CD33 was detectable in 79 percent of myeloid sarcoma tissue rather than all of it, and isolated extramedullary relapse accounted for 46 percent of post-transplant relapses, so an antigen-directed or variant-directed choice made on marrow alone may not cover the thigh lesion. If the biopsy is not feasible, record that limitation in the plan and follow the lesion separately on imaging.
turnaround_estimate: 1-2 weeks for flow and IHC; 2-3 weeks with NGS
tissue_required_estimate: Image-guided core biopsy of the right-thigh lesion; one core in RPMI for flow plus FFPE blocks for IHC and NGS
decision_gated: Whether CD33/CD123-directed and TP53-directed choices made on marrow also cover the extramedullary lesion

providers.name: NeoGenomics Laboratories
providers.notes: Accepts FFPE soft-tissue blocks for both myeloid IHC and comprehensive myeloid NGS, so a single block covers the antigen and variant questions. The biopsy itself is a procedure at the treating centre; interventional radiology there schedules it.

notes: Sequence this against the marrow work rather than in place of it. The comparison, marrow versus thigh, is what carries the information; a thigh result read in isolation answers less.

tissue_type: bone marrow aspirate; archival FFPE or slides acceptable
rationale: Detects the 17p/TP53 copy loss that a 2 percent LOD sequencing panel without copy-number calling cannot see, which is the most mechanical explanation for a negative relapse result in a leukaemia whose 2019 karyotype carried der(17)t(13;17). It also feeds the allelic-state question, since TP53 mutation plus 17p deletion is a multi-hit state that carries its own risk assignment under the 2022 ELN framework. Leaving it out leaves the leading explanation for the 2019-versus-2026 discrepancy untested.
tissue_required_estimate: Bone marrow aspirate (sodium heparin), 2-3 mL; archival FFPE clot or unstained slides acceptable
decision_gated: TP53 copy loss and multi-hit allelic state; supports the TP53-aberrant call and the adverse-risk assignment

providers.name: Mayo Clinic Laboratories
providers.notes: Runs 17p/TP53 FISH as a routine catalogue test on marrow or FFPE with a short turnaround, which is what this row needs.

test_name: p53 protein immunohistochemistry on the marrow biopsy, scored by pattern (overexpression versus complete null)
tissue_type: archival FFPE bone marrow core or clot section
rationale: Adds a protein-level read on material already in the archive, so it costs no new procedure. Pattern-based scoring is what carries the information: strong diffuse nuclear overexpression tracks with missense TP53 mutations and a complete-null pattern with truncating ones, while a normal wild-type pattern argues against a TP53-aberrant state. IHC does not name the variant and its concordance with sequencing is imperfect, so it corroborates rather than substitutes for the variant-level answer the rezatapopt question needs.
tissue_required_estimate: Archival FFPE bone marrow core or clot section; no new procedure required
decision_gated: Corroborates the TP53-aberrant call feeding the rezatapopt decision; not variant-level

providers.name: Mayo Clinic Laboratories
providers.notes: Reports p53 IHC on marrow with pattern-based interpretation, which is the format the myeloid literature validates; a percent-positive-only report is less useful here.

notes: Ask for pattern-based reporting (overexpression, complete null, or wild-type) rather than a simple positive or negative, and read it against the blast percentage, since scattered strong erythroid staining is a known confounder in marrow.

test_name: STR chimerism on flow-sorted CD34+ blasts (recipient versus donor origin)
tissue_type: fresh bone marrow with CD34+ sorting, plus archived donor STR profile
rationale: Confirms that the relapse is recipient-origin leukaemia rather than a donor-derived or therapy-related second neoplasm, which the shared del(5q) and del(7q) lesions suggest but do not prove. The sex-matched sibling donor rules out XY FISH as a shortcut, and unsorted chimerism is diluted by normal donor haematopoiesis, so the analysis has to run on sorted CD34+ cells, where declining donor chimerism precedes haematologic relapse by a median of about two months. A donor-derived leukaemia would redirect the plan toward a different donor rather than toward DLI or HA-directed cells from the same sibling.
tissue_required_estimate: Fresh bone marrow (EDTA) with CD34+ flow sorting, plus the archived donor STR profile from the 2020 transplant
decision_gated: Clonal origin of the relapse; informs HCT2 versus DLI versus alternative-donor strategy

providers.name: Versiti Diagnostic Laboratories
providers.notes: Runs sorted-fraction chimerism as a routine transplant service and can pair it with the HLA LOH evaluation on the same specimen.

notes: Confirm the 2020 donor STR profile is still on file at the transplant centre before drawing; if it is not, a fresh donor sample is needed and that adds weeks.

feature: HLA-restricted immunotherapy handles (HA-1/HA-2 TCR-T, WT1, PRAME) - the primary reason for this Libby run
test_name: HLA loss-of-heterozygosity assessment on sorted blasts (6p LOH by NGS or SNP array) with HLA class I surface expression by flow
tissue_type: sorted blasts from marrow or high-blast blood, with a germline or donor reference
rationale: Asks whether the relapsed clone still presents the restricting allele at all. Genomic HLA loss and transcriptional downregulation of HLA are established routes to relapse after allogeneic transplant, genomic loss having been documented in matched-unrelated as well as mismatched settings, and a blast population that has lost the haplotype carrying HLA-A*02:01 is invisible to every A*02:01-restricted TCR-T and to donor T cells generally, even when germline typing reads positive. Reflex it on sorted blasts once typing returns; skipping it risks committing to a cellular product whose target the leukaemia has already deleted, which is the pattern a late relapse six years after a matched-sibling graft should raise.
tissue_required_estimate: Fresh bone marrow aspirate or high-blast peripheral blood (EDTA) with blast sorting, plus an archived donor or germline reference sample
decision_gated: Whether HLA-A*02:01-restricted TCR-T stays on-target in the relapsed clone; also informs DLI and donor choice for HCT2

providers.name: Versiti Diagnostic Laboratories
providers.notes: One of the few US laboratories advertising HLA LOH evaluation as a service alongside high-resolution typing and chimerism, so the three post-transplant questions route to one account.

providers.name: Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center (Immunogenetics / Bleakley HA-1 program)

notes: Genomic HLA loss is best documented in haploidentical and mismatched-unrelated relapse and is less common after a matched sibling graft, and the NEJM series found downregulation of MHC class II rather than genomic loss as its dominant mechanism. Both possibilities argue for pairing the genomic test with a flow read of surface HLA class I on the blasts.

test_name: Full metaphase karyotype at relapse with MECOM and KMT2A FISH
rationale: Places the MECOM gain and KMT2A amplification reported in 2026 into a complete cytogenetic picture alongside a current metaphase count. MECOM rearrangement and complex karyotype both carry adverse risk under ELN 2022, and many AML trials read karyotype directly as a stratification or eligibility variable. Without a current full karyotype the risk assignment and several trial screens rest on partial data.
turnaround_estimate: 1-2 weeks for karyotype; 3-7 days for FISH
tissue_required_estimate: Fresh bone marrow aspirate (sodium heparin), 2-3 mL, delivered within 24 hours for culture
decision_gated: Adverse-cytogenetics confirmation (MECOM, KMT2A amplification, complex karyotype) for prognosis and trial stratification

providers.name: Mayo Clinic Laboratories
providers.notes: Cytogenetics laboratory with both conventional karyotype and the targeted myeloid FISH probes in one order, so the two results arrive together.

test_name: Germline hereditary myeloid malignancy panel (TP53, DDX41, RUNX1, CEBPA, GATA2, ANKRD26, ETV6 and related genes) on cultured skin fibroblasts
tissue_type: cultured skin fibroblasts from a punch biopsy
rationale: Asks whether an inherited predisposition sits under the MDS-to-AML course, which bears directly on a second sibling-donor transplant: a variant shared with the donor risks donor-derived disease and would redirect donor selection, and a germline TP53 finding would change conditioning intensity and trigger family counselling. Specimen source is the load-bearing detail; with blasts at 58 to 82 percent, blood and saliva cannot give a clean germline call, and the University of Chicago laboratory explicitly declines blood or saliva for this panel in patients with a history of MDS or leukaemia and asks for cultured skin fibroblasts. Skipping it leaves the donor question resting on an assumption at exactly the point where it is being re-made.
tissue_required_estimate: Cultured skin fibroblasts from a 3-4 mm punch biopsy (preferred while blasts circulate); whole blood only if a documented remission sample exists
decision_gated: Sibling-donor selection and conditioning intensity for HCT2; family screening

providers.name: University of Chicago Genetic Services Laboratories
providers.address: 5841 S Maryland Ave, Room G701, MC 0077, Chicago, IL 60637
providers.notes: The reference laboratory for hereditary haematopoietic malignancy panels, and the one that publishes the fibroblast requirement this case turns on. Start the punch biopsy and culture early, since culture is the rate-limiting step.

notes: The biomarker survey raised the same sampling problem under its HRD/BRCA row and routed it to the HLA blood draw. That routing does not work while blasts are circulating; this row supersedes it on specimen choice, not on the underlying question.

tissue_type: whole blood or bone marrow; buccal swab acceptable
rationale: Genotypes the CD33 splicing SNP rs12459419, where the T allele shifts splicing toward a CD33 isoform lacking the IgV domain that gemtuzumab ozogamicin binds. In the randomised COG AAML0531 trial the CC genotype was associated with benefit from gemtuzumab and T-allele carriers were not, though adult confirmation is mixed and the PETHEMA consolidation analysis found no such association, so this reads as context rather than a gate. It adjusts how much to expect from a CD33 antibody-drug conjugate alongside the density result.
tissue_required_estimate: Whole blood or bone marrow; buccal swab acceptable since the result is germline
decision_gated: Refines the expected gemtuzumab ozogamicin benefit; does not gate enrolment or prescribing

providers.name: Hematologics, Inc.
providers.notes: Offers this exact assay as a named clinical test, which is unusual; it also holds the flow specimen for the CD33 density request.
providers.assay_brand: CD33 Single Nucleotide Polymorphism Analysis for Gemtuzumab Ozogamicin Treatment Response

providers.name: ARUP Laboratories
providers.address: 500 Chipeta Way, Salt Lake City, UT 84108

notes: The supporting randomised evidence is paediatric. Adult replication is inconsistent, which is why this sits at medium and why a T-allele result should temper rather than veto a gemtuzumab discussion.
